lines.text: Hm. Clean floors. Good start. Don't get excited, dear, I'm only on the floors.
Closed for days without a sign on the door. In my day we'd have put up a sign. Were you ill, or just careless?
I won't pretend last time was good. It wasn't. Let's see what you do with a second chance.
Your last dish was very good. Don't let it go to your head. Heads are heavy enough.
Afternoon, [wrong name].
I'll take the table by the window. I like to watch the door. Old habit.
[name]. You were closed three days. I worried. ...Don't tell anyone I said that.
Afternoon, [name]. Your floors are still clean. I'm keeping score.
Don't fuss, I'll find my own table. I've been finding my own tables for ninety years.
There you are. I came by twice. The second time I just sat on the bench outside. It's a nice bench.
[name]. Sit with me a minute when you're free. I'm in a talking mood.
I brought you something. A pinch of my own seasoning blend. Don't tell anyone where you got it.
You disappeared on me. At my age, dear, you don't do that to people.
There's my favorite cook. Don't tell Walter. ...He'd agree, actually.
I've decided you're one of mine now. That's not up for discussion.
You said "[last_rude_line]" to me. I've been thinking about it. I expected better.
Afternoon.
Good afternoon, chef.
I know your name, dear. I've always known it. It's on your sign. I just wanted to see if you'd tell me the truth when I got it wrong. You did. That's rarer than you'd think. Thank you, [name].
Thank you, [wrong name]. Same time next week. Maybe sooner.
Goodnight, [name]. Taste everything.
Goodnight, [name]. Thank you for listening to an old lady ramble.
Goodnight, dear. Turn the left burner down.
Thank you.
Foam? On a plate? In my day we called that a mistake.
Hm. ...That's very good. Walter would have asked for seconds.
Edible. Solid. Needs a pinch more salt. You'll get there.
It's burnt, dear. I'm going to eat it, because I don't waste food. But it's burnt.
Thank you, [name]. ...You've improved. I won't say it twice.
You burnt it. Good. Even the best of us do. Walter burnt toast every Sunday for fifty years.
[name], this is as good as anything I ever served. I mean that. I don't say things I don't mean.
Thank you.
Your stove runs hot on the left side. Turn it down a notch. Trust me.
I ran a diner for fifty years. Don't look so surprised. I wasn't always this slow. ...I was always this slow.
Have you seen my glasses? I had them when I came in.
Can I give you some advice? You don't have to take it.
I haven't cooked for anyone since Walter. Not even myself. That's why I come here, I suppose.
That bear with the patches. Stitches. He sits alone every time. Someone ought to say hello to him.
My grandson Cheddar thinks I don't notice his pranks. I notice everything. I let him have it.
You taste everything before it goes out now. I've watched you. That's how I know you'll be fine.
If I had a granddaughter or grandson who cooked like you, I'd be very proud. ...Well. I suppose I do.
Is there something you need, chef? I'm quite comfortable.
